quantity: loss normalization required for lambda_theta(0)=1/4, lambda_phi(0)=M/4
note: lambda_theta(0)=1/4 and lambda_phi(0)=M/4 hold EXACTLY for the MEAN-over-examples (averaged, not summed) binary cross-entropy L = E_Y[log(1+exp(-Y F))] with a single scalar logit F whose per-example margin is q = Y F with unit scaling. Equivalently, the symmetric two-logit softmax convention (F/2,-F/2): its softmax Hessian p(1-p)[[1,-1],[-1,1]] contracted with the logit Jacobian direction (1/2,-1/2) gives the same scalar curvature r(1-r), because only the logit DIFFERENCE (=F) enters. The two normalizations that break the constants: (i) SUMMING instead of averaging over the n training examples / broadcast sites multiplies both blocks by n (e.g. broadcasting to the 2 sites and summing gives 1/2 and M/2); (ii) rescaling the logit (e.g. F/tau) multiplies both blocks by 1/tau^2. D_curv(0)=lambda_phi/lambda_theta=M is invariant under both, since they scale the two blocks identically.
